title: Best Half Marathon Shoes: Racing and Training
excerpt: Half marathon racing and training shoes by goal and pace, plus the best shoes for first-time half marathoners, with list prices.
body:
Best Half Marathon Shoes: Racing and Training

Updated November 2026. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update; retailers often sell for less.

The right half marathon shoe depends on your goal. Faster runners chasing a time benefit most from a plated racing shoe. Most first-timers are better off racing in a cushioned trainer they already know. This guide covers both, plus a section for beginners. It's based on manufacturer specs and published reviews. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update.

Racing shoes

ASICS Metaspeed Edge Tokyo and Sky Tokyo

ASICS makes two versions of its race shoe. The Edge suits runners who speed up mainly by increasing cadence, and the Sky suits runners who speed up by lengthening their stride. The ASICS Metaspeed Edge Tokyo lists at $270 and weighs 159 g as listed by Running Warehouse. The ASICS Metaspeed Sky Tokyo also lists at $270.

Adidas Adizero Adios Pro 4

The Adidas Adizero Adios Pro 4 lists at $250. It has a 39 mm heel stack and a 6 mm drop.

Nike Vaporfly 4 and Alphafly 3

These are Nike's two carbon-plated road racers. The Nike Vaporfly 4 lists at $270. The Nike Alphafly 3 lists at $295.

Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3: race day only

The Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 lists at $500 and weighs about 97 g. It was released in April 2026. It's built for racing only, and the price puts it out of reach for most runners.

World Athletics limits road racing shoes to a 40 mm stack, so these racers sit at or below that limit.

Training shoes for the build-up

  • Hoka Mach X 3 ($190): a neutral trainer with a Pebax plate (not carbon). It suits workouts and long runs at goal pace.
  • ASICS Megablast ($225): a high-cushion super trainer for long runs.
  • Brooks Glycerin 23 ($180): soft, neutral cushioning for easy and long runs.
  • Hoka Arahi 8 ($150): a stability trainer for runners who want more support.
  • Nike Vomero 18 ($155): a well-cushioned daily trainer for easy miles.

Best for beginners

For a first half marathon, choose comfort and fit over speed. Race in a shoe you've already worn on several long runs, so you know how it feels after 10 miles. These cushioned trainers work for both training and race day:

  • ASICS Superblast 3 ($210): light for its cushioning, with an 8 mm drop. Many runners use it to train and race.
  • Hoka Clifton 10 ($155): a cushioned all-rounder with an 8 mm drop.
  • Brooks Ghost 18 ($150): a dependable neutral trainer that comes in several widths.
  • New Balance 1080v15 ($170): a plush, high-stack ride.
  • Adidas Adizero EVO SL ($150): light and unplated, and quick enough to race in.
  • Nike Vomero Plus ($180): maximum cushion from Nike.
  • Hoka Bondi 9 ($175): very high cushioning, with a 5 mm drop.

If you buy a faster shoe for race day, wear it for at least three runs of 8 miles (13 km) or more beforehand. Replace your trainers when the cushioning feels flat or the outsole is worn through, rather than at a set mileage.

Choosing by pace

  • Chasing a fast time: a plated racer, such as the ASICS Metaspeed, Adidas Adios Pro 4 or Nike Vaporfly 4.
  • Mid-pack: a plated racer if you've trained in it, otherwise a light trainer such as the ASICS Superblast 3 or Adidas Adizero EVO SL.
  • First half marathon: the cushioned trainer you've done your long runs in.
